Specialisation: thoracic surgery

Main areas of specialisation:

Dr Boris Gendel is a leading Israeli specialist in lung surgery with almost 40 years of professional experience. He has extensive experience in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the lungs and chest organs, including benign and malignant tumours.

  • Chest surgery
  • Lung surgery
  • Invasive diagnostics
  • Cancer surgery
  • Lung cancer
  • Tumours of the mediastinum and pleura
  • Cardiac surgery
  • Biopsies of the chest organs
  • Spirometry, bronchoscopy, mediastinoscopy and thoracoscopy
  • Lung transplantation

Summary:

Dr Boris Gendel is an accomplished thoracic surgeon and Doctor of Medicine (MD). He is a leading specialist in surgery of the lungs and chest organs in Israel. Over his career he has performed a great many highly complex operations, including lung transplants and robotic surgery, saving the lives of thousands of patients. Dr Gendel is known as an experienced diagnostician who performs procedures such as spirometry, bronchoscopy, mediastinoscopy and thoracoscopy.

Education and clinical experience:

  • Sackler Faculty of Medicine, Tel Aviv University, Israel
  • Fellowship in oncology and radiotherapy, Sheba hospital, Ramat Gan, Israel
  • Specialisation in radiation therapy, radiology department of the Sheba hospital, Ramat Gan, Israel
  • Fellowship in thoracic surgery, Assuta clinic, Tel Aviv, Israel

Academic and research work:

Dr Gendel is actively engaged in research. He is the author of a number of papers published in Israeli and international medical journals. These publications are of great practical value, as they are based on unique clinical experience.

  • Israel Association of Thoracic Surgeons

Dr Cohen is an orthopaedic surgeon specialising in the treatment of conditions of the hip, knee, ankle, shoulder and elbow joints, and of fractures of the limbs. He holds the post of senior physician in the foot and ankle unit of the orthopaedics department at the Ichilov medical centre, and also operates at the Assuta clinic.

His specialisation covers every kind of surgical intervention on the joints, including joint replacement. He performs both primary and revision joint replacement, including complex ankle replacement operations. He uses robotic surgical systems to fit prostheses perfectly, easing patients' recovery and extending the working life of the implants.

In treating fractures he uses individually made supports produced by 3D printing, which are more comfortable than a traditional plaster cast. He successfully treats fractures of any complexity, including those that are slow to unite.

Dr Cohen is also skilled in arthroscopic surgery, carrying out procedures without opening the joint by using endoscopic technique. This includes the reconstruction of ligaments and menisci and the resurfacing of joint surfaces in osteoarthritis.

Another area of his work is the surgical correction of hallux valgus, which he performs using minimally invasive techniques to reduce the trauma of the intervention.

Professor Zvi Ram is rightly considered a veteran of the world of neurosurgery, with more than 30 years of clinical practice to his name, not counting the five years he spent serving in the Israel Defence Forces as a medical officer. He is currently one of Israel's leading experts in neurosurgery. His specialisation includes minimally invasive and complex operations to remove tumours of the brain and the pituitary gland, including procedures approached through the nose and stereotactic radiosurgery. He is also an expert in the treatment of aneurysms, various vascular diseases of the brain, hydrocephalus, severe forms of epilepsy, Parkinson's disease and other neurological conditions.

After completing a six-year fellowship at the Sheba medical centre in Israel, Zvi Ram qualified as a neurosurgeon in 1991. He then spent three years in a fellowship in the United States. On returning home, Ram worked as a senior neurosurgeon for five years, served as deputy head of the neurosurgery department for four, and has headed the department since 2003.

Thanks to Professor Ram, many people have been given a second chance at life. He is also actively engaged in research, having written more than 120 studies that have played an important part in bringing Israeli neurosurgery to the world stage.

An outstanding international specialist in head and neck cancer surgery and in operations on the base of the skull. Since 2003, under his leadership, the head and neck surgery department of the Ichilov medical centre has carried out unique endoscopic operations covering the head, the base of the skull and the cervical region, and has treated complex cases of disease of the inner and middle ear and problems of the throat and nose.

Professor Fliss is actively engaged in research and teaching and takes part in developing modern medical technologies for treating head and neck cancer. The use of an innovative technology, Quicksil bio-glue, brought about a genuine change in thinking about operations on the nose and the paranasal sinuses.

Professor Fliss is the author of 170 research publications and papers in well-known international medical journals. He has also written five books on surgery of the head, the neck and the base of the skull. He heads the department of otolaryngology at Tel Aviv University and is actively engaged in teaching.

Professor Dan Grisaro is recognised in the international medical community as one of the leading experts in cancers of the female reproductive organs. In Israel he is a key figure in this specialisation and has left a marked imprint on the treatment of many women.

Professor Grisaro has the skills and experience to perform complex surgical operations, for example:

  • Diagnostic and therapeutic laparoscopy: a minimally invasive surgical intervention used to examine and treat conditions of the internal female organs.
  • Hysteroscopy: a procedure that allows the inside of the uterus to be viewed for diagnosis or treatment.
  • Dilatation and curettage: removal of tissue from the lining of the uterus.
  • EUA: examination under general anaesthetic to assess the female reproductive organs.
  • Cervical biopsy: a procedure in which tissue samples are taken for microscopic examination.
  • Resection of a leiomyoma: an operation to remove a benign tumour of the uterus.
  • Vaginal and radical hysterectomy: operations to remove the uterus through the vagina or through the abdomen respectively.
  • Removal of the ovaries: an operation to remove the ovaries in whole or in part.
  • Bladder resection with reconstruction: a complex surgical intervention to remove part of the bladder and then reconstruct it.

Professor Grisaro not only makes active use of all these techniques but does so with a high level of skill and professionalism, as his reputation in the medical world confirms.

Professor David Luria is an outstanding cardiologist whose reputation in cardiology and electrophysiology is impeccable. His experience spans more than 35 years, which forms an important foundation for his deep professional knowledge and skill.

  • Fellowship at the Mayo Clinic: the Mayo Clinic is one of the finest medical centres in the world. Completing a three-year fellowship there gave Professor Luria the opportunity to work with, and learn, the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment alongside the world's best specialists.
  • Treatment of atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia by ablation: ablation is a minimally invasive procedure in which small areas of heart tissue producing abnormal electrical impulses are destroyed. The method helps patients avoid surgery and prevents the arrhythmia from returning.
  • Implantation of pacemakers and defibrillators, such as ICDs: an ICD (implantable cardioverter defibrillator) is a device that monitors the heart rhythm and, where necessary, restores it automatically by delivering an electrical impulse.
  • Closure of the left atrial appendage: this method is used to prevent blood clots forming in the left atrial appendage, which reduces the risk of stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation.
  • Transcatheter radiofrequency ablation with CARTO: an innovative technology that uses three-dimensional imaging to locate and destroy the areas of tissue causing the arrhythmia precisely.
  • Ventricular pacing for the treatment of heart failure: a technique that helps improve the work of the heart by correcting the electrical activity between the right and left ventricles.

Professor Luria is a master of all these techniques, and his skill and knowledge make him one of the leading cardiologists in the world. His approach to treating each patient is an individual one, which produces excellent results even in the most complex cases.
